claim: Coached practice on realistic troubleshooting problems (Sherlock 2) lifted novice avionics technicians to master level on trained equipment (VTT3 95 tutored vs 59 control vs 85 masters; N=18/23/13).
agent_test: Compare agent with and without a hint-coached practice set on held-out faults at equal tokens.

claim: Sherlock gains transferred to a different, untrained station (Frankenstation VTT 82 vs 55 control vs 91 masters), but less than on trained equipment.
agent_test: Hold out a whole device family from the case library; measure the gain gap in-family versus out-of-family.

claim: Reported Sherlock effect sizes of 1.27 and 1.17 SD cannot be reproduced from the table (control SD gives about 0.97 and 0.89) because control SDs are huge; the effect is real but about 1 SD.
agent_test: Report effect sizes with pooled SD and report variance, not only means.

claim: Tutored novices used the self-test efficiently (2 of 14 uses inefficient vs 11 of 16 for controls): training changed strategy, not just recall.
agent_test: Log whether the agent's test choices follow a split-half order after case exposure.

claim: Experts and novices differ in strategic knowledge, not procedural skill; a guide hides the training effect (Hydrive problem A vs B).
agent_test: Test with and without an explicit strategy hint; the hint should shrink the case-library benefit.

claim: Intelligent tutoring systems help on average: median +0.66 SD (50 evaluations) and g=0.42 vs large-group teaching (107 effect sizes), but not versus individual human tutoring (g=-0.11, n.s.).
agent_test: Use as prior: expect scaffolding to match a good human, not exceed it.

claim: Human case-library studies show mixed effects: failure cases, retain versus retrieval/reuse prompts and indexing prompts change outcomes; retrieval/reuse prompts were worse than none in one study.
agent_test: Vary what is stored (success vs failure) and whether retrieval is forced; compare at equal tokens.

claim: Retrieving past cases improves LLM agents: Memento case memory gives +6.7 F1 on DeepResearcher (59.9 to 66.6) and about +5 to +9 on out-of-distribution sets.
agent_test: Add a case bank to our agent; run held-out items. All numbers come from one lab and one paper.

claim: Returns of case retrieval saturate quickly: K=4 is best (F1 64.5), K=1 already gets 63.6, K=32 gets 63.9.
agent_test: Sweep K=1,2,4,8 at equal context budget; expect a plateau near 4.

claim: Distilled memory items beat raw trajectories: ReasoningBank 48.8 vs AWM 44.1 vs Synapse 42.1 vs none 40.5 on WebArena (Gemini-2.5-flash); also for Pro (53.9 vs 46.7) and Claude-3.7 (46.3 vs 41.7).
agent_test: Store distilled strategy items, not raw logs; compare to raw-trace retrieval.

claim: Failure cases help only when distilled: ReasoningBank gains from failures (success-only 46.5 to 49.7 with failures; no memory 39.0), Synapse small (+1.1), AWM loses (44.4 to 42.2). Baseline concern in a24 resolved (d17).
agent_test: Include failed attempts with a diagnosis line; ablate by dropping failures.

claim: Memory and test-time compute multiply: with memory, parallel k=5 raises 49.7 to 55.1; without memory the same scaling is flat (39.0-42.2).
agent_test: At equal total tokens, split budget between k samples and memory retrieval.

claim: Workflow memory induced from experience raises web-agent success: AWM WebArena 35.5 vs 23.5 (+12.0), and gains grow with train-test gap; ReasoningBank replicates the direction against AWM as baseline.
agent_test: Induce workflows from solved items; test gain against novelty of test items.

claim: Reflection on experience adds to episodic memory alone: Reflexion +22 ALFWorld, +20 HotpotQA; ExpeL insights plus retrieval 59.0 vs ReAct 40.0 on ALFWorld.
agent_test: Two arms: raw-case retrieval vs retrieval plus written insight.

claim: How cases are selected matters: ExpeL ALFWorld task-similarity 59.0, reasoning-similarity 48.5, random 42.5, no cases 40.0. Random sampling nearly erases the gain.
agent_test: Compare similarity retrieval vs random cases at same count. Note c18 had the labels in the wrong order.

claim: Insights from experience transfer across tasks: HotpotQA to FEVER 58 to 63-70; insights-only (36/50/37) and retrieval-only (31/55/38) each help, retrieval better on ALFWorld.
agent_test: Cross-domain transfer test of the case library.

claim: Memory quality control matters: naive add-all memory drifts below an error-free baseline; history-based deletion can beat it.
agent_test: Run repeated sessions with and without pruning; track accuracy over episodes.

claim: Structured historical-incident retrieval (OM-RAG) scored 0.931 diagnosis accuracy vs 0.325 chunk retrieval vs 0.238 none on 1,172 LLM-judged issues; groundedness did not predict accuracy.
agent_test: Index cases by symptom-to-cause structure rather than by text chunk.

claim: RCACopilot: retrieving similar past incidents plus handler evidence gives micro-F1 0.766 vs 0.026 for prompt only; about 25% of incidents have causes not seen before.
agent_test: Also measure the novel-cause slice, where retrieval must not force a match.

claim: Case reuse does not always help agentic diagnosis: Cloud-OpsBench trajectory ICL helped OnlineBoutique (JRA 0.70 to 0.79) but not TrainTicket (0.58 to 0.56) and hurt some models; runbook distillation was mixed.
agent_test: Report per-model and per-system gains; add an abstain-on-poor-match rule.

claim: LLM diagnosis failures are mostly premature stopping: 73% of incomplete cloud investigations stopped at the symptom log; GPT-5 was correct but evidence-incomplete in 33.1% and 29.4%.
agent_test: Require a source-tracing step before verdict; measure evidence-complete rate.

claim: AI tutoring without guardrails can harm: GPT Base cut unaided exam scores 17% while GPT Tutor with guardrails did not; a guarded AI tutor RCT (N=194) gave effect about 0.63.
agent_test: Check that a case or hint helper does not replace the agent's own derivation (answer-copy rate).

claim: LLM access did not improve physician diagnosis in an RCT (76% vs 74%, CI -4 to 8) although the LLM alone scored 92%: having the tool is not using the tool.
agent_test: Check that the agent's use of retrieved cases is audited, not assumed.

claim: No independent replication of the Jonassen case-library effect in humans was found. The Hernandez-Serrano and Jonassen (2003) abstract reports a win on multiple-choice process questions only, with no short-answer difference. The Tawfik group studies (N=22 to 91) and one outside indexing-prompt study (Park 2020, N=105) are small, argumentation-based and not about fault diagnosis.
agent_test: Treat human case-library results as hypotheses; test on the agent.

claim: Case-based RAG gave a small gain on legal QA: cosine 0.9141 vs 0.8967 (N=32, Mistral-7B).
agent_test: Do not rely on it; tiny sample.

claim: A lightweight text memory (Dynamic Cheatsheet) also gives large test-time gains: Claude 3.5 Sonnet AIME 2024 23% to 50%; GPT-4o Game of 24 10% to 99%.
agent_test: Compare to a case bank at equal tokens; check for answer leakage in Game of 24.

claim: Wrong or conflicting stored memory is followed in about two thirds of first steps and costs 10 to 26 points of success, and agents rarely recover (re-alignment 7 to 15 percent).
agent_test: Inject a plausible wrong case in a diagnosis test and measure harm; add a verify-before-act step.

claim: A wrong stored lesson costs 15 to 25 points of task success (lesson kept 40 percent vs removed 55 vs corrected 65), and 16 percent of ReasoningBank lessons were wrong-but-consistent; a verify step before storing cut this to 5 percent.
agent_test: Gate case admission with a verifier; log case provenance and error rate.

claim: Add-all case memory is worse than a small fixed memory (CIC-IoT diagnosis 59.9 vs 71.5; strict admission 85.4); pruning by history cut records 904 to 188 with no loss.
agent_test: Admit only verified cases; prune by use history; cap bank size.

claim: A gate that rejects past experience before reuse cut harmful reuse from 100 to 25 percent while keeping 90 percent of useful items, but this was tested on fine-tuning updates, not prompt-time case retrieval, and not on diagnosis.
agent_test: Test an abstain-on-poor-match rule on Cloud-OpsBench; note relevance gating gave no gain in WebArena (d03).

claim: Independent runs of the ReasoningBank/AWM family give smaller or uneven gains than the originals: tau2-bench +2.6 (76.4 to 79.0) for ReasoningBank; EvoMemBench shows gains on execution tasks (28.5 to 43.0 at 16K) but a stronger memory-free model beats every memory method in many cells.
agent_test: Treat published memory gains as upper bounds; measure on our own diagnosis set.

claim: At comparable tokens, memory is not clearly better than a stronger base model: memory methods used up to 3.6 times the tokens (202,966 vs 55,787) and often lost. No study compares a case library with self-consistency at equal tokens for fault diagnosis.
agent_test: Run case library vs self-consistency at equal total tokens on Cloud-OpsBench.

claim: Abstract or insight-level records transfer better than raw trajectories to harder tasks (forward transfer insight +6.5 and +9.0 vs raw -9.5 and -7.5); a sparse index can send 88.5 percent of queries to one item. In diagnosis retrieval, shape similarity is a weak proxy (NDCG@10 0.49 vs 0.69 with labelled reranking).
agent_test: Index by cause and strategy with a difference note; compare to symptom-only indexing.

claim: Prompting learners to index cases by explanation or by difference raised self-explanation and rebuttal scores (N=105), whereas prompting to retrieve and reuse was worse than no prompt in Tawfik 2017. Human indexing evidence is thin and not about fault diagnosis.
agent_test: Store a one-line why-it-matches and how-it-differs note with each case.

claim: Gains from stored experience rise with task similarity (r=0.72 Gemini, 0.56 Claude) and with number of stored episodes when retrieval is over raw episodes (51.7 to 66.0 going from 1 to 4); summaries do not scale. Exact-match success overstates transfer by about 50 points.
agent_test: Report results separately for repeat vs novel faults; start the bank with repeat-style faults.

claim: Memory and a structured plan can be super-additive: planner 28.5 to 29.7, memory 30.1, both 33.5 percent on SWE-bench Verified (interaction p=0.011). Agent structure alone is not additive for all models in RCA (Plan-and-Execute worse than Straight-Shot for small models).
agent_test: Use the state machine to gate when the bank is consulted; ablate scaffold x bank.

claim: Automatically built experience stores nearly match hand-written ones (GAIA 75.15 vs 76.97; SWE-bench Lite 51.0 vs 55.7) but still hurt in some cells (-7.7).
agent_test: Auto-build the bank from agent runs; keep expert cases as a check set.

claim: Giving memory only after a first failed attempt gave +10.4 on WebArena vs +1.3 for always-on helpful memory, and closed 96 to 101 percent of the gap to an oracle schedule.
agent_test: Consult the case bank only after the first hypothesis fails.
